gqa_28q_sweep.reading: time flat in kv_heads at 28 query heads

evidence.l2_effect: the unique KV slab (kv * kv_heads * (qk+v) * 2) decides the achieved rate: at 128 query heads / kv=32768 the slab is 71 MB (fits 192 MB L2) and kv_heads 1->8 raises time only 1.38x for 8x the declared bytes
evidence.why: at fixed 28 query heads the decode time is flat in kv_heads (2.0% spread at kv=32768 and kv=126976), so traffic cannot be proportional to kv_heads; with 7 query heads kv_heads 1 vs 7 is flat to 1.3%, i.e. the same 7 streams either way

byte_model.observed: kv * q_heads * (qk_dim + v_dim) * dtype (KV streamed once per query head)
byte_model.recommendation: use observed bytes (q_heads) for long-KV decode; the current artifact's kv_broadcast=4 gives max(4, ceil(28/4))=7 streams for 28Q/4KV (already correct) but only max(1, ceil(7/4))=2 for the TP4-local 7Q/1KV shard where 7 are observed

conclusions: All rows were measured on die 4 (Phy-ID 4, NPU 2 chip 0) with the AICore at its rated 1650 MHz under load; the measured HBM copy stream is 1247 GB/s, so the observed-byte decode rates of 1.21-1.24 TB/s are 97-99% of the achievable HBM stream.

A3 accepts the same fused-attention contracts as A5: BNSD sparse_mode=3 decode and TND varlen sparse_mode=3 + 2048 mask causal prefill; npu_fused_infer_attention_score does not accept the BNSD spelling.

A3 long-KV decode streams KV once per query head: at 28 query heads the time is flat in kv_heads (2.0% spread at kv=32768 and 126976), and at the TP4-local 7 query heads kv_heads 1 vs 7 is flat to 1.3%.

Measured decode rate under the observed (q_heads) byte base is 1.10-1.15 TB/s for 28Q/4KV (eta 0.92-0.96) and 0.73-0.87 TB/s for the 7Q/1KV shard at batch>=4 (eta 0.61-0.73); batch 1 is parallelism-limited (0.21 TB/s at 7Q).

The current A3 attention row's additive kv_token_ms walk (2.0014e-5 ms per visible KV) matches the measured batch-1 7Q shard op (2.54 vs 2.15 ms at kv=126976) but is charged per request, so a c8 step is over-charged 4.85x (568 ms vs 117 ms measured-implied); the row's eta_memory 0.218 is also 4.2-4.4x below the measured stream eta.

So the 21x long-context gap is an eta/rate and batch-additivity defect of the additive token-latency tail plus a 4.2x low eta_memory - not the A5-style declared-vs-observed byte-base defect: kv_broadcast=4 already declares 7 streams for 28Q/4KV. The residual byte-base gap is only the TP4-local 7Q/1KV shard (2 declared vs 7 observed streams).
